title: The Due column reads 1 day and ordinal days correctly for the shop's terms
custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as a user with the "Admin" role, working in {Location-A}.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • The shop has its own active terms: {Term-A} due 1 day after the invoice date, {Term-B} due 365 days after, and day-of-the-following-month terms {Term-C} (day 1), {Term-D} (day 2), {Term-E} (day 3), {Term-F} (day 11), {Term-G} (day 12), {Term-H} (day 13), {Term-J} (day 21), {Term-K} (day 22), {Term-L} (day 23) and {Term-M} (day 31).
    For example: {Term-A} is ZZAUTOTEST S1-11 N1, {Term-B} is ZZAUTOTEST S1-11 N365 and {Term-C} to {Term-M} are ZZAUTOTEST S1-11 D1, D2, D3, D11, D12, D13, D21, D22, D23 and D31.
  • Starting screen: the Credit Terms page (Settings, then "Credit Terms" in the Finance group) is open on the Active tab.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: {Term-A} reads "1 day after the invoice date" (singular); {Term-B} reads "365 days after the invoice date"; {Term-C} "1st of the following month", {Term-D} "2nd of the following month", {Term-E} "3rd of the following month", {Term-F} "11th of the following month", {Term-G} "12th of the following month", {Term-H} "13th of the following month", {Term-J} "21st of the following month", {Term-K} "22nd of the following month", {Term-L} "23rd of the following month", {Term-M} "31st of the following month".

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Credit terms", Confluence 963346440, version 3 (22 Oct 2026, "Renamed to Credit terms", Chris Ward), read 23 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11638, story SV-11670 (Story 1, Credit Terms page and list)

  • S1-R7: “The Due column describes each term in words:”
  • S1-R7, a Net term: “A Net term: "{X} days after the invoice date" ("1 day after the invoice date" when X is 1), for example "30 days after the invoice date"”
  • S1-R7, a day of the following month term: “A "day of the following month" term: "{ordinal day} of the following month", for example "10th of the following month", "1st of the following month", "22nd of the following month"”
  • Key Decisions: “Net terms run from 1 to 365 days.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

References from Design

Design canvas "Default Credit Terms" (https://claude.ai/artifact/2erYxWz2ffDNcoXzEfu6wf), read 23 Oct 2026: page "1 List and row menus" ("Active tab: one table"). Compare the screen with the pictures below; the expected results above come from the PRD quotes.

Design pictures attached to this case:

The design's own words:

  • “Due wording: COD "Paid when the invoice is created"; Due on Receipt "Due on the invoice date"; Net X "X days after the invoice date"; day of month "10th of the following month"; Credit Hold "Invoicing is blocked".”
